what: Domain vocabulary (use these exact terms in plots, docs and messages)
title: CLAUDE.md — Rceattle
text: Match vocabulary axis labels, documentation, console messages; don’t substitute lay phrasing. Reference points: Amendment-56 SPR proxies — F40% = max FABC, F35% = FOFL, B40% = BMSY proxy (Tier 3); Tier 1 uses estimated FMSY/BMSY. Don’t write “MSY” SPR proxy meant. SSB = female spawning-stock biomass. “Recruitment deviations” (log-scale), “recruitment error”. Selectivity: name form — logistic / double-normal / gamma / nonparametric / semi-parametric. Don’t call every dome shape “double-normal”. Composition: age comps, length comps, conditional age--length (CAAL). ageing-error matrix applies age/CAAL data fit; length-stocks none. Data weighting: Francis (2011), McAllister–Ianelli, Dirichlet-multinomial. Diagnostics: Mohn’s rho (retrospective), OSA residuals, likelihood profiles.

title: 6. Building a data object in R
code: library(Rceattle)  # Define core dimensions up front, these drive the size of all downstream arrays. nspp     <- 2   # number of species (or stocks) nages    <- 10  # maximum age classes (same for all species here) nlengths <- 20  # number of length bins (for age-length keys / CAAL data) nyrs     <- 30  # number of hindcast years years    <- 1:nyrs  simData <- list()

title: 6. Building a data object in R
text: scalars vectors describe biological structure species control population model used.
code: simData$nspp    <- nspp simData$styr    <- 1       # first year of hindcast simData$endyr   <- nyrs    # last year of hindcast simData$projyr  <- nyrs + 10  # last year of the projection period  # Character labels shown in plots and output tables simData$spnames <- paste0("Species", 1:nspp)  # nsex: 1 = combined-sex model (male and female treated as one group), #        2 = sex-structured model (separate selectivity and mortality by sex) simData$nsex    <- rep(1, nspp)  # Calendar month of spawning, used to compute the fraction-of-year weight # applied to spawning stock biomass (e.g., 6 = mid-year spawning) simData$spawn_month <- rep(6, nspp)  simData$nages   <- rep(nages, nspp)   # number of age classes per species simData$minage  <- rep(1, nspp)       # minimum age (usually 1) simData$nlengths <- rep(nlengths, nspp)  # estDynamics controls how population abundance is estimated: #   0 = estimate population dynamics (standard statistical catch-at-age) #   1 = fix N-at-age exactly to values in NByageFixed (e.g., external estimates) #   2 = scale NByageFixed by a single estimated scalar per species simData$estDynamics <- rep(0, nspp)  # Indices linking each species to its weight and growth datasets. # Multiple weight schedules can exist (e.g., fleet-specific); these point to # which one is used for total biomass (pop) and spawning biomass (ssb). simData$pop_wt_index <- 1:nspp simData$ssb_wt_index <- 1:nspp simData$pop_age_transition_index <- rep(1, nspp)  # Length-weight relationship coefficients: W = alpha * L ^ beta. # Used internally to convert length-based selectivity to weight when estimating growth. simData$alpha_wt_len <- rep(0.00001, nspp) simData$beta_wt_len  <- rep(3, nspp)  # Prior or initial standard deviation for log-recruitment deviations. Controls the # strength of the recruitment penalty in penalized-likelihood mode. simData$sigma_rec <- rep(1, nspp)  # Non-modeled ("other") prey biomass available to predators. Used in # multi-species mode to prevent unrealistically high predation mortality when # modeled prey are scarce. Setting this too low forces predators to over-eat # modeled prey; too high dilutes the predation signal. simData$other_food <- rep(1e5, nspp)   # metric tons of non-modelled prey

title: 6. Building a data object in R
text: row defines one fleet (fishery survey) controls modeled. Multiple fleets can target species.
code: # Fleet_type: #   "Fishery", contributes catch and catch-at-age/length composition data #   "Survey", contributes an abundance index and composition data #   "Off", fleet is present in the data but excluded from the likelihood  # Selectivity options (Selectivity column), use the string name or integer code: #   "Fixed"              (0), fixed at values in emp_sel; not estimated #   "Logistic"           (1), two-parameter ascending logistic (a50, slope) #   "NonParametric"      (2), freely estimated selectivity-at-age/length with smoothness penalty #   "DoubleLogistic"     (3), ascending + descending dome-shaped logistic #   "DescendingLogistic" (4), descending logistic only (dome-shaped for oldest ages) #   "Hake"               (5), non-parametric selectivity à la Taylor et al. (Pacific hake) #   "2DAR1"              (6), 2D autoregressive random effects (bin × year) #   "3DAR1"              (7), 3D autoregressive random effects (bin × year × cohort) #   "DoubleNormal"       (8), Gaussian ascending/descending limbs blended at peak #   "NonParametricPM"    (9), Ianelli non-parametric, ADMB AMAK penalty #   "LogisticPM"        (11), AMAK logistic with multiplicative deviations #   "NonParametricIntegrable" (13), deviations with a proper density (random_sel) #   "DoubleNormalSS3"   (15), SS3 size pattern 24, six-parameter #   (sel_map in R/0-switches.R is the registry; 10, 12 and 14 are unused) # # Selectivity_dimension: "Age" or "Length" #   Length-based selectivity requires an age-to-length transition matrix (see below).  # Catchability options (Catchability column), use the string name or integer code: #   "Fixed"                (0), Q fixed at Catchability_init; not estimated #   "Estimated"            (1), freely estimated on log scale #   "Estimated-with-prior" (2), estimated with a lognormal prior (Catchability_init, Catchability_prior_sd) #   "Analytical"           (3), Walters & Ludwig (1994) analytical Q #   "PowerEquation"        (4), NOT YET IMPLEMENTED; data_check() refuses it #   "AnalyticalArith"      (7), arithmetic-mean analytical Q #   "Environmental"        (5), mu_q + X * beta, where X is a covariate in env_data #   "AR1"                  (6), REMOVED in 5.12.0; data_check() errors. Use a q #                                  linkage with ar1(1 | Year) and observe = <column> #   NA, not applicable (use for fisheries without CPUE)  # Comp_distribution / CAAL_distribution options: #   "Multinomial", standard multinomial #   "DirichletMultinomial", overdispersed; estimates a concentration parameter #   "MultinomialAFSC", AFSC variant of multinomial (marginal age + length)  simData$fleet_control <- data.frame(   Fleet_name  = paste0(c("Survey", "Fishery"),                        rep(paste(" Species", 1:nspp), each = 2)),   Fleet_code  = 1:(nspp * 2),       # unique integer ID per fleet   Fleet_type  = rep(c("Survey", "Fishery"), nspp),   Species     = rep(1:nspp, each = 2),   Month       = 0,                   # 0 = not specified; read for comps and                                      # weight-at-age when growth is estimated    # Selectivity_index links fleets that share the same selectivity curve.   # Fleets with the same index share all selectivity parameters.   Selectivity_index         = 1:(nspp * 2),   Selectivity               = "Logistic",   Selectivity_dimension     = "Age",   N_sel_bins                = NA,    # used for NonParametric only   Sel_curve_pen1            = NA,    # smoothness penalty (NonParametric)   Sel_curve_pen2            = NA,   # Time_varying_sel:   #   0 / "Off" = time-invariant (default)   #   1 / "IID" = penalized log-normal deviates (SD fixed at Time_varying_sel_sd   #       unless random_sel = TRUE in fit_mod)   #   2 / "AR1" = REMOVED in 5.16.0; data_check() errors on it   #   3 / "Block" = time blocks (specify via R-side mapping)   #   4 / "RandomWalk" = random walk   #   5 / "RandomWalkAscending" = random walk on ascending portion of double logistic   Time_varying_sel          = 0,   Time_varying_sel_sd = 1,   Bin_first_selected        = 1,     # first bin selected; selectivity is 0 below it   Sel_norm_bin             = "Off", # "Max", "Off", or a bin to normalize at   Sel_norm_bin_upper       = "Off", # "Off", or the top of a bin range   # Two-sex models only: whether the normalization reference is pooled over the   # sexes ("AcrossSexes", default, keeps relative sex selectivity) or taken per   # sex ("WithinSex", both sexes reach 1, only the shape differs).   Sel_norm_scope           = "AcrossSexes",    # Composition likelihoods   Comp_distribution = "Multinomial",   Comp_weights = 1,                  # input effective sample size multiplier   CAAL_distribution = "Multinomial",   CAAL_weights = 1,    # Index units and weight/growth linkage   Observation_units     = 1,          # 1 = weight (mt), 2 = numbers   Weight_index         = rep(1:nspp, each = 2),   Age_transition_index = 1,    # Catchability_index links fleets that share the same catchability parameter.   Catchability_index              = 1:(nspp * 2),   Catchability         = rep(c("Estimated", NA), nspp),   Catchability_init              = rep(c(1,   NA), nspp),   Catchability_prior_sd           = rep(c(0.2, NA), nspp),   # Time_varying_q:   #   0 / "Off" = time-invariant   #   1 / "IID" = penalized log-normal deviates (SD fixed at Time_varying_q_sd   #       unless random_q = TRUE in fit_mod)   #   2 / "AR1" = REMOVED in 5.16.0; data_check() errors on it   #   3 / "Block" = time blocks   #   4 / "RandomWalk" = random walk   Time_varying_q          = rep(c(0, NA), nspp),   Time_varying_q_sd = rep(c(1, NA), nspp),    # Estimate_index_sd:   #   0 = fix at Log_sd from index_data   #   1 = estimate a single SD   #   2 = analytical sigma (Walters & Ludwig 1994)   Estimate_index_sd  = rep(c(0,  NA), nspp),   Index_sd     = rep(c(1,  NA), nspp),    # Estimate_catch_sd:   #   0 = fix at Log_sd from catch_data (treats catch as known)   #   1 = estimate   #   2 = analytical sigma (Walters & Ludwig 1994); concentrates the sd out of   #       the catch likelihood, so catch stops pinning F as tightly   Estimate_catch_sd  = rep(c(NA, 0),  nspp),   Catch_sd     = rep(c(NA, 1),  nspp),    # Proj_F_proportion: how future F is distributed across fishery fleets per species.   # Must sum to 1 across fishery fleets for each species. NA for surveys.   Proj_F_proportion = rep(c(NA, 1), nspp) )

Observation biomass index natural scale – mt, thousands fish Observation_units = 2 – log. likelihood takes log , data_check() requires positive. negative Year value tells Rceattle predict index without including likelihood, useful model checking.

what: 8. Multi-species bioenergetics parameters (optional in single-species mode)
title: 6. Building a data object in R
text: parameters govern Wisconsin bioenergetics model used compute predation mortality (M2) multi-species mode. single-species mode reach reported ration consumption_at_age, never objective, can omitted entirely; Rceattle fills missing scalars safe defaults (Ceq = 4, constant form reads environmental index). multi-species mode (msmMode > 0) Ceq, Cindex, Pvalue, fday, CA, CB, Qc, Tco, Tcm, Tcl, CK1, CK4 must supplied length-nspp vectors; data_check() list missing wrong-length. Likewise diet_data ration_data required. See ?build_M1 CEATTLE technical documentation full details parameter.
code: # Ceq: consumption (bioenergetics) equation form for each species: #   1 = Exponential (Stewart et al. 1983) #   2 = Warm-water temperature dependence (Kitchell et al. 1977) #   3 = Cool/cold-water temperature dependence (Thornton & Lessem 1979) #   4 = bypass bioenergetics; use ration_data directly (set CA = 1, fday = 1, CB = 0) simData$Ceq    <- rep(4,  nspp)  simData$Cindex <- rep(1,  nspp)   # which env_data covariate column drives it, counting from 1 simData$Pvalue <- rep(1,  nspp)   # proportion of maximum consumption realised simData$fday   <- rep(1,  nspp)   # foraging days per year  # Wisconsin model coefficients (CA, CB) and temperature dependence parameters simData$CA  <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$CB  <- rep(-1, nspp) simData$Qc  <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$Tco <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$Tcm <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$Tcl <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$CK1 <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$CK4 <- rep(1,  nspp)  # Diet composition likelihood for each predator species # 0 = Multinomial, 1 = Dirichlet-multinomial simData$Diet_distribution      <- rep(0, nspp) simData$Diet_comp_weights <- rep(1, nspp)  # Ration data (optional in single-species mode): observed mean ration-at-age from # bioenergetics studies. Required when msmMode > 0. Skip in single-species mode. # # When provided, columns are: Species, Sex, Year, Age1, ..., Age<nages>.  # Diet composition data: observed stomach content proportions (predator-prey pairs). # Required when msmMode > 0; skip in single-species mode. # # When provided, columns are: Pred, Prey, Pred_sex, Prey_sex, Pred_age, # Prey_age, Year, Sample_size, Stomach_proportion_by_weight.

title: 6. Building a data object in R

code: plot_data(simData) # Key fit_mod() arguments: # # estimateMode: 0 = full fit (hindcast + projection) #               1 = hindcast only #               2 = projection only (fix parameters, run HCR) #               3 = evaluate only (MakeADFun, no optimisation), useful for debugging # # msmMode:      0 = single-species, 1 = Type II MSVPA, 2 = Type III MSVPA # # initMode:     0 = freely estimated initial N-at-age #               1 = equilibrium, F_init = 0, no init deviations #               2 = equilibrium, F_init = 0, with init deviations (default) #               3 = non-equilibrium: F_init estimated, init devs included #               4 = non-equilibrium: F_init scales R0 #               5 = equilibrium, F_init = 0, seeded by R_init displaced by the #                   year-1 recruitment deviation, no init deviations #               6 = non-equilibrium: F_init weighted by fishery selectivity at #                   age (SS3's InitF convention); the only mode that reads an #                   initial equilibrium catch at styr - 1 # # phase:        TRUE = use parameter phasing for improved convergence (recommended)  sim_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = simData,   # simData carries caal_data, which is the age composition within a length bin   # and so is predicted from growth: it needs a parametric growth model, per the   # requirements table above.   growthFun    = build_growth(fun = "vonBertalanffy"),   estimateMode = 3,    # change to 0 for a real fit   msmMode      = 0,   initMode     = 2,   random_rec   = FALSE,   fit_control = fit_control(     phase        = TRUE,     verbose      = 1))

title: Environmental linkages and priors
text: Environmental drivers (temperature, prey density, climate indices) enter stock assessments recruitment, natural mortality, growth, catchability, selectivity. Rceattle holds long-format linkage table: one row per estimated coefficient tying design column process parameter. Describe linkage linkage_spec(), formula-driven helper, pass relevant build_*() function; process applies resulting offset parameter, year year. linkage path wired growth (von Bertalanffy Richards), natural mortality (M1), recruitment (R0, alpha, beta, R_init), catchability (q), selectivity (form’s parameters), , prior-, Dirichlet-multinomial composition weights.

title: Environmental linkages and priors
text: Von Bertalanffy growth K responding temperature index, one slope per species sex (whamGrowthData one , one slope ): fits Ks,sex,y=Ks,sexeβs,sextempyK_{s,\mathrm{sex},y} = K_{s,\mathrm{sex}}\,e^{\beta_{s,\mathrm{sex}}\,\mathrm{temp}_y} species ss; pieces fit together gives general form.
code: library(Rceattle) data(whamGrowthData) plot_data(whamGrowthData)  # Use logistic selectivity for all fleets in this example. whamGrowthData$fleet_control$Selectivity <- "Logistic" whamGrowthData$fleet_control$Selectivity_dimension <- "Length"  # 1. Attach an env_data table to the data list. Must include `Year` #    plus whatever covariates show up in your formulas. Here `temp` is #    a placeholder; in real use it would be a standardized SST series, #    PDO index, etc. yrs <- whamGrowthData$styr:whamGrowthData$endyr whamGrowthData$env_data <- data.frame(   Year = yrs,   temp = rnorm(length(yrs), 0, 0.1) )  # 2. Build a growth specification with one linkage per parameter that #    you want to vary. linkage_spec() captures one process parameter's #    formula, strata (by / species / sex / fleet), link, init, bounds, #    priors, random-effect handling (formula terms, integrate) and any #    state-space covariate (observe, obs_sd, obs_sd_est). ?linkage_spec #    documents each. growth_spec <- build_growth(   fun = "vonBertalanffy",   linkages = list(     K = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ temp,             # 2 columns: (Intercept) and `temp`       by      = ~ species + sex,    # one beta per (species, sex, column)       priors  = list(temp = normal(0, 0.1)) # Tight prior     )   ) )  # 3. Fit as usual. fit <- fit_mod(   data_list   = whamGrowthData,   growthFun   = growth_spec,   estimateMode = 0,    msmMode     = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(verbose = 0) ) summary(fit)

code: # Prior on the SD at L1 anchored at exp(log(5)) = 5 length units, # with a tight normal prior on the log scale. growth_spec_sd <- build_growth(   fun = "vonBertalanffy",   linkages = list(     sd_L1   = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,       by      = ~ species + sex,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 5),       # Prior on log-scale SD; switch to `normal(5, 0.3)`       # for a Normal on sd_L1.       priors  = list(`(Intercept)` = lognormal(log(5), 0.3))     ),     sd_Linf = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,       by      = ~ species + sex,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 15)     )   ) )  # After fit_mod(), the init values set the SD at L1 and the SD at Linf # (on the log scale), and the priors evaluate against those SD # parameters via the intercept re-targeting path described above. rec_spec <- build_srr(   srr_fun = 0,   linkages = list(     R0 = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,       by      = ~ species,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 1000),       # Species-keyed priors on log-scale R0.       priors  = list(`(Intercept)` = list(         `1` = lognormal(log(1000), 0.2),         `2` = lognormal(log(1500), 0.3),         `3` = lognormal(log(800),  0.25)       ))     )   ) ) fit$quantities$jnll_comp["Linkage-table priors", ] fit$data_list$linkage_table[fit$data_list$linkage_table$param == "K", ] fit$estimated_params$beta_linkage          # (Intercept) rows are 0; slopes are estimated fit$estimated_params$log_growth_pars       # base K / L1 / Linf / m (on log scale internally) data("GOApollock") # Using GOA pollock as an example  # One-species model, lognormal(log(0.34), 0.01) prior on M1 # applied via the linkage intercept (equivalent to a Normal on log_M1). # The structural M1_model is kept at "sex_age_invariant" (= 1). M1_spec <- build_M1(   M1_model = "sex_age_invariant",   linkages = list(     M1 = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,       by      = ~ species,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 0.34),       # Prior is on the natural-scale for M1.       # `lognormal(log(0.34), 0.01)` evaluates Normal on log(M1).       # Use `normal(0.34, 0.01)` for a Normal directly on natural M1.       priors  = list(`(Intercept)` = lognormal(log(0.34), 0.01))     )   ) )  # Fit the model - no manual mapping needed fit <- fit_mod(   data_list = GOApollock,   M1Fun     = M1_spec,   estimateMode = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(phase = TRUE) )

text: formula passed linkage_spec() fed straight stats::model.matrix(), expression understands works: polynomial bases, splines, interactions, arithmetic transformations. Polynomials. poly() gives orthogonal basis poly(..., raw = TRUE) raw monomials. order design column coefficient: poly() orthogonalises every row env_data supplied, including beyond projection horizon, columns zero-mean span linear slope, quadratic curvature estimated independently. Prefer unless scientific reason want raw monomials. Arbitrary arithmetic. Use () insert literal expression (otherwise temp^2 interpreted formula crossing operator reduces temp): design column name deparsed call ((temp^2)), init, bounds priors must key string — backticks let write name. Splines. splines::ns() gives natural cubic splines: flexibility without high-order polynomial’s tail behaviour: Interactions. temp:PDO adds single product column; temp * PDO shorthand temp + PDO + temp:PDO: Mixing forms across species. per-species formula machinery one species can take polynomial response another linear one, without duplicating columns: -named columns must numerically identical across specs use . Deterministic formulas evaluated one env_data give automatically; specs built different env_data frames can break .

title: 4. Projections and reference points
code: library(Rceattle)  data(BS2017SS) data(BS2017MS)  # Set the terminal projection year BS2017SS$projyr <- 2060 BS2017MS$projyr <- 2060  # Plot input data plot_data(BS2017SS)  # Fit baseline single- and multi-species models ss_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017SS,   inits        = NULL,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 0,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(     phase        = TRUE,     verbose      = 1))  ms_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017MS,   inits        = ss_run$estimated_params,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 0,   niter        = 5,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 1,   suitMode     = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(     verbose      = 1))

title: 4. Projections and reference points
text: estimateMode = 2 runs projection period , holding estimated parameters fixed, specified harvest control rule. build_hcr(HCR = 2, Ftarget = ...) sets constant F species. several fisheries target species, Proj_F_proportion column fleet_control splits projected F across fleets. values must sum 1 per species.
code: BS2017SS$fleet_control$Proj_F_proportion <- 1  # One fishery fleet per species BS2017MS$fleet_control$Proj_F_proportion <- 1  ms_run_proj <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017MS,   inits        = ms_run$estimated_params,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 2,   HCR          = build_hcr(HCR = "ConstantF",                             Ftarget = c(0.2342936, 0.513, 0.0774777)),   niter        = 5,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 1,   suitMode     = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(     verbose      = 1))  plot_catch(ms_run_proj, incl_proj = TRUE)

title: 4. Projections and reference points
text: Projection recruitment deviations live parameter list, can overwrite directly projecting. estimateMode = 3 evaluates model without re-estimating anything, updated deviations change projection.
code: nyrs      <- BS2017MS$endyr - BS2017MS$styr + 1 nyrs_proj <- BS2017MS$projyr - BS2017MS$styr + 1 yrs_proj  <- (nyrs + 1):nyrs_proj  # Replace future rec_devs with draws from N(0, 0.707) ms_run$estimated_params$rec_dev[, yrs_proj] <- stats::rnorm(   n    = length(ms_run$estimated_params$rec_dev[, yrs_proj]),   mean = 0,   sd   = 0.707 )  ms_run_proj2 <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017MS,   inits        = ms_run$estimated_params,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 3,   # Evaluate only, do not re-estimate   niter        = 5,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 1,   suitMode     = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(     verbose      = 1))

title: 4. Projections and reference points

title: 5. Single- vs. multi-species models
text: Single-species appropriate : Predation interactions unknown negligible species interest major predators prey system building initial model debugging data inputs Multi-species appropriate : Predation important source mortality (e.g., groundfish Bering Sea Gulf Alaska) want evaluate climate-driven changes predator prey abundance propagate food web Reference points account ecosystem effects common workflow fit single-species models first use estimates starting values (inits) multi-species run.

title: 5. Single- vs. multi-species models
text: niter argument controls many times population dynamics predation mortality equations iterated convergence within gradient step. Five iterations typically sufficient.
code: library(Rceattle)  # BS2017SS and BS2017MS use the same data structure but differ in M1_base: # the multi-species dataset has lower residual mortality because some of # that mortality is explained by predation (M2) in multi-species mode. data(BS2017SS) data(BS2017MS) BS2017SS$projyr <- 2060 BS2017MS$projyr <- 2060  plot_data(BS2017SS) # Single-species ss_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017SS,   inits        = NULL,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 0,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 0, # <-- single-species   fit_control = fit_control(     phase        = TRUE,     verbose      = 1))  # Multi-species, start from single-species MLEs for stability ms_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017MS,   inits        = ss_run$estimated_params,  # warm start   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 0,   niter        = 5,        # iterations between population and predation dynamics   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 1,        # <-- Type II MSVPA   suitMode     = 0, # empirical suitability from diet data   fit_control = fit_control(     verbose      = 1))

what: Rceattle — Multispecies Stock Assessment in R
title: Rceattle — Multispecies Stock Assessment in R
text: Rceattle: R package fitting climate-linked, single- multi-species age-structured stock assessment models testing via diagnostics, simulation, management strategy evaluation. Rceattle implements models R using Template Model Builder (TMB; Kristensen et al., 2015). Data can supplied via bundled Excel template constructed programmatically R list (see Building data object without Excel vignette). Capabilities include: Single-species (msmMode = 0) multispecies (msmMode > 0) configurations, one- two-sex population dynamics One multiple stocks can fit jointly. Multiple fisheries surveys range catchability selectivity parameterizations (logistic, double-logistic, non-parametric, time-varying, etc) Stock–recruitment options (Beverton–Holt, Ricker, mean-recruitment, environmentally-driven) Estimable growth (von Bertalanffy / Richards/ empirical weight--age) Environmental linkages priors recruitment, natural mortality, growth parameters Bioenergetics-based predation input temperature-specific consumption (multispecies mode) Forward projections alternative harvest control rules climate scenarios Closed-loop MSE, retrospective, jitter, simulation testing Tidy outputs via S3 methods (.data.frame, coef, logLik, vcov, residuals, plot) See browseVignettes("Rceattle") package website full documentation. Installation operational / management use, pin specific tagged release rather tracking main, e.g.: maintainer email DESCRIPTION (grant.adams@noaa.gov) preferred contact questions package; please open issue bug reports feature requests discussion publicly searchable. Getting started 1-species model Fit 2018 Gulf Alaska pollock model, inspect fit, plot : 3-species model Fit three single-species model jointly Bering Sea data: multispecies model, set msmMode = 1. See package vignettes (browseVignettes("Rceattle")) projections, alternative harvest control rules, MSE testing, model diagnostics, non-Excel data construction. deeper context, see onboarding document Wiki. model can updated following instructions . Examples Additional code function examples using data Bering Sea Gulf Alaska groundfish applications can found examples folder include: * Fitting single-species models * Fitting multi-species models * Estimating growth * Alternative HCRs MSE testing * Simulation * Model diagnostics References Adams, G.D., Holsman, K.K., Barbeaux, S.J., Dorn, M.W., Ianelli, J.N., Spies, ., Stewart, .J., Punt, .E., 2022. ensemble approach understand predation mortality groundfish Gulf Alaska. Fish. Res. 251, 106303. doi:10.1016/j.fishres.2022.106303 Holsman, K. K., Ianelli, J., Aydin, K., Punt, . E., & Moffitt, E. . (2016). comparison fisheries biological reference points estimated temperature-specific multi-species single-species climate-enhanced stock assessment models. Deep Sea Research Part II: Topical Studies Oceanography, 134, 360-378. Kristensen, K., Nielsen, ., Berg, C. W., Skaug, H., & Bell, B. (2015). TMB: automatic differentiation Laplace approximation. arXiv preprint arXiv:1509.00660. Wassermann, S. N., Adams, G. D., Haltuch, M. ., Kaplan, . C., Marshall, K. N., & Punt, . E. (2025). Even low levels cannibalism can bias population estimates Pacific hake. ICES Journal Marine Science, 82(1), fsae064.
code: # Rceattle (pulls CRAN dependencies automatically) install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("afsc-assessments/Rceattle")  # Optional: TMBhelper provides richer optimization diagnostics. # Rceattle falls back to plain nlminb + sdreport if it's not installed. # remotes::install_github("kaskr/TMB_contrib_R/TMBhelper") remotes::install_github("afsc-assessments/Rceattle@5.66.1") library(Rceattle)  # Gulf of Alaska pollock data (1977-2018) data(GOApollock) plot_data(GOApollock)  # Fit the hindcast fit <- fit_mod(   data_list    = GOApollock,   estimateMode = 0,                              # 0 = fit hindcast + projection   fit_control  = fit_control(phase = TRUE)       # optimizer / sdreport / phasing knobs )  # S3 methods: the fit behaves like an R model object fit                       # compact print summary(fit)              # same compact summary coef(fit)                 # estimated fixed-effect parameters logLik(fit)               # logLik with df attribute (AIC works) AIC(fit) vcov(fit)                 # fixed-effect covariance from sdreport as.data.frame(fit)        # return data.frame of derived quantities  # Plot dispatcher: pick a panel with `what` plot(fit, what = "biomass") plot(fit, what = "ssb") plot(fit, what = "recruitment") plot(fit, what = "index")  # Residuals across data sources (long-format data frame) ix_resid   <- residuals(fit, source = "index")                  # title: Specify the harvest control rule (HCR) used for Rceattle — build_hcr
text: HCR Harvest control rule, integer string alias: 0/"NoFishing" (catch, hindcast ), 1/"CMSY" (maximize joint catch, optionally holding depletion Plimit), 2/"ConstantF" (constant input F Ftarget), 3/"ConstantFSSB" (F reaching Ftarget percent SSB0 end projection), 4/"ConstantFSPR" (constant Fspr, scalable Fmult following NEFSC), 5/"NPFMC", 6/"PFMC" 7/"SESSF". Default 0. 0, 1, 2, 3 6 work multispecies mode. DynamicHCR TRUE/FALSE. Use dynamic rather static reference points (default FALSE). Ftarget Target fishing mortality rate (yr^-1), SPR- depletion-based, input F projections. SPR F40%, enter 0.40. Flimit Limit fishing mortality rate (yr^-1), SPR- depletion-based. SPR F35%, enter 0.35. Ptarget Target spawning-stock biomass proportion static dynamic spawning-stock biomass F = 0. B40%, enter 0.40. Plimit Limit spawning-stock biomass basis. B10%, enter 0.10. Alpha Parameter used NPFMC Tier 3 rule. Pstar Quantile uncertainty buffer, given Flimit Sigma. Sigma Standard deviation normal uncertainty buffer, given Flimit Pstar. Fmult Multiplier target F (default 1), scaling following NEFSC convention. HCRorder multispecies models, order project fishing (predators first, prey, instance).

text: hcr = 5 "NPFMC", North Pacific Fishery Management Council Tier 3 spawner-per-recruit rule: Stock status: \(SB > SB Ftarget\) $$Fofl = Flimit$$ $$Fuse = Ftarget$$ Stock status: \(Alpha < SB / SB Ftarget \le 1\) $$Fofl = Flimit * (SB / SB_{Ftarget} - Alpha) / (1 - Alpha)$$ $$Fuse = Ftarget * (SB / SB_{Ftarget} - Alpha) / (1 - Alpha)$$ Stock status: \(SB / SB Ftarget \le Alpha\) \(SB < Plimit * SB0\) $$Fofl = 0$$ $$Fuse = 0$$ hcr = 6 "PFMC", Pacific Fishery Management Council category 1 40-10 annual catch limit rule (PFMC 2020), using Fspr single species F reaching X% SSB0 predation. uncertainty buffer qnorm(Pstar, Flimit, Sigma), equals Flimit + qnorm(Pstar, 0, Sigma) sits Flimit \(Pstar < 0.5\). taper runs \(SB0 * Plimit\) \(SB0 * Ptarget\), 40-10 shape needs Ptarget = 0.40 Plimit = 0.10; default Plimit = 0 gives 40-0 rule. Stock status: \(SB > SB0 * Ptarget\) $$Fofl = Flimit$$ $$Fuse = qnorm(Pstar, Flimit, Sigma)$$ Stock status: \(SB0 * Plimit < SB \le SB0 * Ptarget\) $$Fofl = Flimit$$ $$Fuse = qnorm(Pstar, Flimit, Sigma) * \frac{SB0 * Ptarget * (SB - SB0 * Plimit)}{SB * SB0 * (Ptarget - Plimit)}$$ Stock status: \(SB < SB0 * Plimit\) $$Fofl = 0$$ $$Fuse = 0$$ hcr = 7 "SESSF", Southern Eastern Scalefish Shark Fishery Tier 1 spawner-per-recruit rule, F_Limit = F_(20%) B_Limit = SB_20 (AFMA 2017): Stock status: \(SB > SB0 * Ptarget\) $$Fofl = Flimit$$ $$Fuse = Ftarget$$ Stock status: \(SB0 * Ptarget > SB > SB0 * Plimit\) $$Fofl = Flimit * (SB / (SB0 * Plimit) - 1)$$ $$Fuse = Ftarget * (SB / (SB0 * Plimit) - 1)$$ Stock status: \(SB < SB0 * Plimit\) $$Fofl = 0$$ $$Fuse = 0$$

Default = 0 srr_pred_fun Stock-recruit function used projection, reference points penalties. srr_fun == 0 curve added penalty annually estimated hindcast recruitment (AMAK / Jim Ianelli pollock form); srr_fun > 0 equals srr_fun penalty added. proj_mean_rec Recruitment used projection: TRUE/1 (default) mean recruitment hindcast, FALSE/0 follows srr_pred_fun. Equilibrium dynamic reference points follow curve whenever srr_pred_fun stock-recruit form, whatever set . srr_mse_switchyr Year MSE switches annual recruitment-penalty estimate stock-recruit function. srr_hat_styr, srr_hat_endyr First last year used estimate recruitment-penalty function (active srr_pred_fun > 0 srr_fun = 0), defaulting styr + 1 endyr. Set environmental data conditioning curve span full series projections still wanted. srr_est_mode curve's built-prior, code string: 1 / "Estimated" (default, prior), 2 / "LognormalPrior" 3 / "BetaPrior" Beverton-Holt steepness, single-species . 0 / "Fixed" Ricker "LognormalPrior" deprecated favour alpha linkage. srr_prior Natural-scale prior mean Beverton-Holt steepness modes 2 3 (median lognormal prior bias_adjust_proc = FALSE). uses, Ricker alpha prior, fixed alpha, alpha's starting value, deprecated. srr_prior_sd Prior standard deviation: log scale lognormal prior (mode 2), natural scale beta prior (mode 3). srr_alpha_init, srr_beta_init Optional natural-scale starting values alpha beta, one per species, used curve estimates . srr_indices Defunct: supplying error; express environmental effect linkages. Bmsy_lim Upper limit Ricker SSB-MSY (1/beta) metric tons, adding likelihood penalty estimated SSB-MSY rises . Default NA unused. linkages Named list linkage_spec() objects keyed "R0", "alpha", "beta" "R_init" – note key unitless log-scale MULTIPLIER initial age structure, reported quantity R_init, equilibrium recruitment F = F_init thousands fish. recommended way put prior , fix, add environmental effect parameters. See vignette("environmental-linkages--priors").

title: Specify the stock-recruit relationship (SRR) for Rceattle — build_srr
text: None starting values knows stock's scale, bad one fails fit rather fitting badly. Mean recruitment (R0) starts \(e^9 = 8103\) thousand fish; alpha starts srr_prior (default 4) wherever alpha \(e^3\) otherwise; beta starts 3. Set srr_alpha_init / srr_beta_init linkage init. \(\beta\) sets density dependence \(R = \alpha S / (1 + \beta S)\), must order \((\alpha - 1/\phi_0) / R_0\), typically \(10^{-3}\) smaller stock measured tonnes. Starting three orders magnitude away drives predicted recruitment near zero optimizer returns NA/NaN gradient evaluation. steepness \(h\) unfished spawning biomass per recruit \(\phi_0\): $$\alpha = \frac{4h}{\phi_0 (1 - h)}, \qquad       \beta  = \frac{\alpha - 1/\phi_0}{R_0}.$$ predation, \(\phi_0\) undefined, seed curve fitted earlier fit's SSB-recruitment pairs.

what: Plot composition fits and residuals — plot_comp
title: Plot composition fits and residuals — plot_comp
text: Diagnostic plots age / length composition data fitted Rceattle model, drawn ggplot2 consistent look plot.rceattle_osa(). default residual_type = "pearson" three figures produced per fleet x composition type: Pearson residual bubbles year bin, faceted fleet (, joint-sex data, sex); red = positive, blue = negative, sized magnitude. Pearson residual form used residuals.Rceattle(), standardized variance fleet's likelihood assumes, weight column Dirichlet-multinomial overdispersion already denominator. Annual composition: observed (shaded area) vs fitted (line) proportion age / length, one panel per year. Joint-sex data mirrored (females , males ). Aggregated composition: observed vs fitted, counts pooled fitted hindcast years. interval holds 95% data model predicts (confidence interval mean), observations outside indicate misfit. Poor expected count 10, slightly narrow throughout, treats fitted proportions known rather estimated data. shaded area fitted line span observed bins (extend past first/last bin), bins zero observed proportion retained (NA bins dropped), curves interpolated across gaps.

title: Process residuals for an Rceattle model's random-effect processes — process_residuals
text: One-sample process residuals model's random-effect (penalized) process deviations, style SAM's procres() (Nielsen Berg 2014). validate process model, whether deviations behave like assumed iid normal process, complement observation-based osa_residuals(). set deviations holds Gaussian process prior model. posterior mode deviations shrunk toward prior, , following SAM, single draw taken joint posterior deviations (joint precision random effects, fixed-effect covariance penalized fixed effects) standardized process standard deviation. correctly specified process approximately iid N(0, 1). random draw used residuals stochastic; set seed reproducibility. Supported processes deviations: "recruitment" rec_dev, prior N(-bias_adjust_proc * R_sd^2/2, R_sd^2) per species. "initial" init_dev, prior N(-bias_adjust_proc * R_sd^2/2, R_sd^2) per species. "catchability" index_q_dev, prior N(0, q_dev_sd^2) per index. "" returns every supported process present fit. Selectivity natural-mortality deviations (use random-walk / 2D-AR1 priors) yet supported. Recruitment initial-abundance residuals exact (priors iid). Catchability residuals exact iid deviate prior (Time_varying_q = 1 2); random-walk AR1 catchability prior marginal-SD standardization ignores prior correlation, residuals approximate warning emitted.

title: Residuals from an Rceattle fit — residuals.Rceattle
text: Residual kinds (type): "response" Observed minus fitted. index / catch log scale default (matching lognormal likelihood; set scale = "natural" arithmetic difference); comp / caal difference proportions, observed minus fitted. "pearson" Standardized residuals. catch log-scale survey index, \((\log o - (\log\hat{o} - b\,\sigma^2/2))/\sigma\) using model's realized observation log-SD \(\sigma\) observation bias-adjustment flag \(b\) (bias_adjust_obs, default 1). natural-scale index fleet (Index_distribution "MVN", "MVNORM", "Normal" "TruncatedNormal") holds ABSOLUTE \(\sigma\) standardized \((o - \hat{o})/\sigma\) instead. Two caveats : covariance fleet ("MVN", "MVNORM") takes \(\sigma\) sqrt(diag(index_cov)), since likelihood never reads reported scalar sd, gets marginal residual rather whitened one (use type = "osa" ); "TruncatedNormal" standardized untruncated moments, approximate \(\hat{o}/\sigma\) small enough truncation shift mean. comp / caal, \((p - \hat{p})/\sqrt{\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p})/N}\) input sample size N. "osa" One-step-ahead residuals via osa_residuals(), builds composition observation data demand fit. Pass arguments ...; note method = "cdf" forms conditional mean, Fitted NA every row . "process" Process residuals via process_residuals() model's random-effect deviations; source apply. Composition rows returned long form (one row per observation x age/length bin) hold Age0_Length1 flag comp_data (0 age, 1 length); CAAL rows hold conditioning Length age Bin. fleet uses tail accumulation (Comp_accum_young / Comp_accum_old), composition residuals describe bins likelihood actually fit: tails folded boundary bin bins outside window reported, model never fit separately. Bin names age length residual belongs Accumulated marks boundary bins, stand range rather single bin named . Fleets without accumulation unchanged.

Internal rename – model results unchanged (four reference models stay bit-identical), fit_mod() loads renamed DLL automatically. fit built custom fit_control(TMBfilename = ...) unaffected. Caveat: object fitted earlier version stores TMBfilename = "ceattle_v01_11", re-running osa_residuals() saved fit needs re-fit version first (old DLL name longer built).

title: Rceattle 5.0.5
text: Moved ?build_selectivity prior example @examples (previously rendered broken \verb{}); corrected ?build_hcr PFMC notation use normal quantile qnorm() rather Phi (denotes CDF); regrouped 4.10.0 linkage additions New features. Minor vignette / README fixes.

title: Rceattle 5.0.4
text: Random-effect models phase without flat-field NaN. phasing, deviates random effect (recruitment, selectivity, catchability, …) now estimated penalized fixed effects variance / correlation hyperparameters held, Laplace approximation switched final hindcast fit. Previously deviates integrated first phase, random field started flat (-zero); 2D AR1 selectivity (random_sel = TRUE), integrating flat field gives NaN marginal objective fit start without external warm start. Phasing deviates penalized effects first builds realistic non-zero values, final Laplace begins near mode. Gated presence random effects, fits without unchanged (four reference models remain bit-identical).

title: Rceattle 5.0.3
text: OSA residuals now support every survey-index likelihood family. osa_residuals() previously produced one-step-ahead residuals lognormal IID index (Index_distribution "Lognormal"). now covers families: natural-scale "Normal" residualizes independent normal natural scale, correlated covariance families "MVN" / "MVNORM" whitened lower Cholesky fleet’s survey covariance Sigma = L L', residuals multivariate-Gaussian one-step-ahead innovations L^-1 (obs - q*pred) — closed form TMB::oneStepPredict() reproduces Gaussian block (Thygesen et al. 2017). supersedes 5.0.2 exclusion fleets. ordinary model fit unchanged (whitening applies post-hoc OSA observation vector). String aliases fit_mod() mode switches. estimateMode msmMode now accept readable names alongside integer codes: estimateMode = "Estimate" (0), "Hindcast" (1), "Projection" (2), "DebugBuild" (3), "DebugOptimize" (4); msmMode = "SingleSpecies" (0), "MSVPA" (1), "TypeIIIMSVPA" (2). integer codes still work, unrecognized string errors valid options listed.

title: Rceattle 5.0.2
text: OSA residuals longer silently mis-residualize non-lognormal index fleets. osa_residuals() / build_osa_data() previously laid MVN-covariance (Index_distribution “MVN”/“MVNORM”) natural-scale “Normal” survey observations one-step-ahead observation vector independent lognormals, even though C++ likelihood families read OSA observation vector — producing invalid residuals warning. fleets now excluded OSA residuals warning naming ; lognormal (IID) index fleets model unaffected. (Covariance-aware OSA residuals MVN families separate follow-.)

title: Rceattle 5.0.1
text: OSA residuals now support composition tail accumulation. fleet folds age/length composition tails via Comp_accum_young / Comp_accum_old (AFSC ac_yng/ac_old), osa_residuals() now residualizes folded composition actually fit – one residual per fitted (folded) bin per sex block, rather refusing combination. build_osa_data() applies per-sex-block young/old fold OSA observation vector, one-step-ahead decomposition matches fitted composition likelihood bin--bin. Fleets without accumulation unchanged.

title: Rceattle 5.0.0
text: Also covers unreleased 4.14.0 development increment, whose entries folded section.

title: Rceattle 5.0.0
text: mse_summary() now returns per-entity list instead one stacked data.frame. result list(species, fleet, total, meta): species (one row per species, keyed Species) holds conservation/status metrics; fleet (one row per fishery fleet) holds average catch / catch IAV / P(Closed); total across-fleet totals; meta carries run provenance. removes NA padding ambiguity old shape, species, fleet, “” rows stacked one frame column like Average Catch meant different things per row. metric values unchanged. Update summ$"<metric>" call sites summ$species$"<metric>" summ$fleet$"<metric>".

title: Rceattle 5.0.0
text: Fixed ConstantFSPR harvest control rule (HCR = 4) applying Fmult twice, set projected F Ftarget * Fmult^2. now Ftarget * Fmult. affects projections Fmult != 1 (default Fmult = 1 unchanged). Corrected documented reference-point formulas ?build_hcr: SESSF (Tier 1) NPFMC (Tier 3) fishing-mortality ramps PFMC 40-10 buffer (normal quantile function, CDF). Restored plot_logindex() deprecated shim plot_index(log = TRUE). forwards plot_index() .Deprecated() notice.

title: Rceattle 5.0.0
text: Plus-group SD--age convention (build_growth(sd_plus_group=)). estimated growth, choose oldest age class’s standard deviation length--age set: "WHAM" (default) pins upper anchor exp(sd_Linf) (WHAM SDAA convention, unchanged prior releases); "SS3" instead interpolates length like interior age. Per-species (scalar length-nspp), round-trips save_config()/load_config(), affects growth_model > 0 fits. Existing models bit-identical default.

title: Rceattle 4.13.1
text: NA-handling diagnostic check_caal_data() now reports “CAAL data NAs …” instead mislabeling “Composition data” (message copy-pasted check_composition_data()). Message text ; change data fit. model_average(uncertainty = TRUE) longer opens plot device partway computation. stray plot_ssb() call fired averaged sdrep$sd populated, drew stale, pre-averaging confidence intervals unrequested side effect; averaged object returns unchanged.

title: Rceattle 4.13.0
text: Save / load run configuration (save_config() / load_config()). full run configuration – [model_config()] structure plus estimation controls fit_control() bundle – round-trips documented, git-diffable YAML file (field carries doc string comment; fields default omitted two runs diff real differences). Apply saved config fit_mod(data_list, config = load_config("run.yaml")); fills arguments caller pass (explicit argument always wins), every fit now records run configuration used (fit$run_config, also reachable via run_config(fit)). Follows SAM’s saveConf/loadConf config-separate--weights idiom; adds yaml dependency. Composition tail accumulation (AFSC ac_yng / ac_old). Two new fleet_control columns, Comp_accum_young Comp_accum_old, fold young old tails fleet’s age/length composition boundary bin composition likelihood (per sex block joint-sex comps), every composition family including default MultinomialAFSC. 1-based bin ordinals fleet’s composition dimension; leaving unset (young = 1 / old last bin) applies accumulation, every existing model bit-identical. data_check() rejects --range inverted (young > old) bins, OSA residuals available fleet active accumulation (residuals built un-accumulated bins).

title: Rceattle 4.13.0
text: self_test() longer errors object 'getsd' found. per-simulation refit closure referenced getsd value function – unlike retrospective(), jitter(), profile() – never defined, every simulation died sequential parallel-cluster path. self_test() now takes getsd argument (default NULL, inheriting input model’s setting) like sibling functions.

title: Rceattle 4.12.0
text: Intuitive fleet_control / data column names. workbook data-list columns renamed say hold, keeping back-compat alias upgraded read, existing data lists, .rda, workbooks, scripts keep working (one-time deprecation message) fit identically: Q_index/Q_init/Q_sd_prior → Catchability_index/Catchability_init/Catchability_prior_sd; Comp_loglike/CAAL_loglike/Index_loglike → Comp_distribution/CAAL_distribution/Index_distribution; Sel_norm_bin1/Sel_norm_bin2 → Sel_norm_bin/Sel_norm_bin_upper; weight1_Numbers2 → Observation_units; proj_F_prop → Proj_F_proportion; control scalar sigma_rec_prior → sigma_rec; bioenergetics Diet_loglike → Diet_distribution; post-fit output column Est_weights_mcallister → Comp_weights_mcallister (old name still written downstream readers). write_template(). new export writes minimal, structurally complete single-species starter workbook canonical column names; round-trips read_data() builds fit_mod(estimateMode = 3). Single-source workbook schema. column dictionary now lives package (R/0-column_schema.R) drives switch_check() defaults, write_data() object order, embedded meta_data documentation sheet, roxygen field dictionary, kept sync guard tests. ~16 previously used--undocumented columns now documented.

title: Rceattle 4.12.0
text: read_data() names offending sheet cell instead failing cryptically. required sheet (control, fleet_control) named absent, optional sheets skipped, minimal single-species workbook reads cleanly. non-numeric cell control bioenergetics rows named rather silently becoming NA. rearrange_data() likewise fails clearly malformed fleet_control rather via cryptic dplyr error. Removed dead accumulation-age feature. Accumulation_age_lower/upper range-validated never applied composition data; dropped (soft-deprecation message old workbook carries ).

title: Rceattle 4.11.0
text: initMode = "OffsetEquilibrium" (5). new initial-age-structure mode: F = 0 equilibrium seeded first-year recruitment (R_init * exp(rec_dev[year 1])) decayed residual natural mortality M1, initial deviates turned init-dev penalty. Unlike initMode = "Equilibrium", sits initial equilibrium recruitment R_init, initial numbers track year-1 recruitment deviation, matching AFSC GOA pollock (Cole Monnahan) convention — first-year cohort initial numbers--age share one deviation. name refers offset; equilibrium unfished. Note deviation enters single scalar every age, moves level initial numbers--age without changing proportions--age. Every mode unchanged (golden references bit-identical). Priors base selectivity parameters linkage grammar. selectivity linkage intercept-formula priors entry now places prior base logistic parameter carries level — ascending/descending slope (slp_asc / slp_desc, log_sel_slp, log scale) inflection (inf_asc / inf_desc, sel_inf, natural scale), e.g. build_selectivity(linkages = list(inf_asc = linkage_spec(~ 1, priors = list(\(Intercept)` = normal(0, 3))))). Uselognormal()log-scale slopes andnormal()natural-scale inflections. mirrors prior-onlybuild_composition()path reproduces AFSC GOA pollock selectivity priors. (Previously intercept prior silently inert selectivity — thesel` process missing prior re-targeting.) Per-predator suitability reference years (suit_styr / suit_endyr). fit_mod() arguments (underlying data_list fields) now accept vector length nspp predator can average suitability different set years — e.g. California Current model hake 1980–2019, arrowtooth 2013–2018, sablefish 2005–2008. single scalar recycled every predator, exactly reproducing previous global-window behavior (BS2017MS golden references unchanged numerical tolerance). Internally suit_styr / suit_endyr became per-predator DATA_IVECTORs suitability-averaging stomach-content prediction loops index predator. plot_diet_comp2() plot_diet_comp1(). plot_diet_comp2() adds aggregation-aware diet-composition diagnostics (line plots prey- predator-age aggregated, dodged bars , bubble grids fully disaggregated), built residuals(source = "diet"). plot_diet_comp1() alias plot_diet_comp() (bubble/grid diagnostic).

title: Rceattle 4.11.0
text: read_data() tolerates trailing empty age columns NByageFixed. Older writers pad fixed numbers--age sheet wider age range max(nages); -NA trailing columns now dropped read instead tripping data_check() column-count validation. Parallel workers now run -session package. run_mse(), retrospective(), jitter() use FORK cluster non-Windows platforms, workers run parent’s loaded namespace via copy--write. fixes silently running stale installed package workers pkgload::load_all() development sessions, removes per-worker startup cost. Parallel serial runs stay bit-identical given seed; Windows keeps previous PSOCK path fallback.

title: Rceattle 4.10.0
text: Random-effect linkages (~ (1 | group)). linkage formula may now carry IID random effect, parameter can vary year year (grouping) set deviations damped estimated N(0, sigma) density, rather fixed covariate slopes: level grouping variable gets one deviation (beta_linkage_re); distinct group estimates log-SD (log_sigma_linkage). density reported new jnll_comp row “Linkage random effects”. deviation SD routed linkage_spec() arguments every parameter: init = list(sigma = v) fixes input value (reproducing legacy Time_varying_*_sd_prior fixed input), priors = list(sigma = lognormal(...)) places prior estimates — first prior deviation SD anywhere model. data_requirements() — see inputs model configuration needs. new exported reader reports, given model spec, top-level data inputs Required, Optional (used supplied, otherwise default-filled clean_data()), Ignored (consulted feature switched ) — conditions data_check() enforces fit time, surfaced front instead buried validator: accepts either existing (possibly partial) data list convenience switch arguments; explicit switch argument overrides data list’s stored value (matching fit_mod() precedence). Internally, data_check()’s conditional presence-requirement gates refactored consume one declarative requirement table, reader validator can never drift apart. build_data() — assemble data list R. code-first constructor complementing read_data(): supply blocks model uses optional blocks single-species model need default-filled clean_data(). Three combinable entry points cover workflows real assessments use: Overrides checked recognized schema, typo (maturty) caught construction suggestion rather surfacing later fit; legacy names (fsh_biom, srv_biom, wt, pmature, Pyrs) mapped canonical equivalents. Validation deferred data_check() fit time (one source truth); build_data() runs light presence pre-check missing required block reported early. result bare list read_data() returns round-trips write_data() unchanged — build_data(base = X) object fits bit-identically X. model_config() — model configuration travels data. model-structure arguments fit_mod() (msmMode, initMode, HCR build_*() process specifications) can now bundled slot data list, data object records meant fit: fit_mod()’s signature defaults unchanged; data list carries model_config, fit_mod() reads field arguments caller pass (detected missing()), explicitly-passed argument always overrides slot. slot present behavior byte-identical (BS2017SS fit bit-identical). call passes argument — even default — overrides slot, omit argument let configuration take effect. slot code-side structure, workbook sheet, persist write_data()/read_data() round-trip (warning fires). Spec-tree print() / summary() data objects fits. build_data() object now carries class "Rceattle_data" prints indented specification tree — dimensions → fleets (selectivity / catchability forms mirroring) → configured processes → active linkages → attached model_config() — instead dumping ~40-element list. tree shown print() fitted model fit statistics, “read 600 lines switch tables” becomes “read printout”. class thin tag: every consumer still treats object plain list, change fit. Random-walk linkages (rw(1 | group)). deviation follows random walk — N(0, sigma) successive first differences, first deviate pinned walk’s level stays base parameter — reproducing Dorn-style Time_varying_* = "RandomWalk" process grammar. grouping variable must numeric (real elapsed-time lag). AR1 linkages (ar1(1 | group)). stationary first-order autoregressive deviation, SCALE(AR1(rho), sigma) sigma marginal SD rho correlation (glmmTMB convention, form Rogers et al. (2024) QAR1 catchability process). correlation routed grammar sigma: init = list(rho = 0.7) fixes , priors = list(rho = normal(0, 0.3)) places prior , else estimated free. Reduces IID density rho = 0. State-space environmental covariate (Rogers et al. 2024 QAR1). ar1(1 | Year) term can turned measured latent covariate via observe / obs_sd: AR1 latent observed env_data column fixed measurement SD, enters linked parameter estimated effect size. reproduces Rogers-2024 QAR1 catchability model (Estimate_q = 6) grammar: AR1 process, covariate observation, effect size carried one term; observe requires ar1 term positive fixed obs_sd. Priors Dirichlet-multinomial data weights (build_composition()). DM likelihood self-tunes composition dataset’s effective sample size, weight can poorly identified fleet comp years. new build_composition() linkage attaches prior DM weight, keeping implied effective sample size believable range without reverting Francis / McAllister–Ianelli hand-tuning: Keys theta_comp / theta_caal / theta_diet cover age/length composition, conditional age--length, predator diet. process prior-(weight scalar, year-varying): covariate, init, est_phase composition spec, linkage fleet/predator fit DirichletMultinomial likelihood, errors front. Formula-linkage effect sizes now reported. estimated linkage coefficients (beta_linkage), random-effect deviations (beta_linkage_re), Rogers-2024 QAR1 effect size (beta_linkage_obs) appear fit$quantities, coefficients / effect size ADREPORT’d carry standard error sdreport. Previously QAR1 effect size — quantity model exists estimate — buried raw parameter vector readable exposure uncertainty. QAR1 covariates need span whole series. state-space observe covariate (e.g. survey index began mid-series) now handled without hand-padding: env_data auto-extended start styr NA missing years, latent AR1 spans hindcast years, observation applied covariate present (un-observed years masked — fabricated observations, unlike legacy mean-fill). Fixed-effect covariates must still finite model range: missing year fixed-effect (non-observe) covariate now errors clearly rather silently producing NaN. QAR1 observation SD can fixed estimated. Rogers-2024 observe / obs_sd state-space covariate holds measurement SD fixed default; pass linkage_spec(..., obs_sd_est = TRUE) estimate (one per observed group, started obs_sd), reference Estimate_q = 6 / GOApollock model . Estimation opt-freely-estimated obs_sd collapses toward 0 smooth covariate (effect-size / obs_sd identifiability degeneracy) — keep fixed unless covariate informative (prior obs_sd regularise future work). Selectivity penalties can given standard deviations. cryptic penalty weights Sel_curve_pen1/2/3 can instead supplied SDs via Sel_shape_sd (+ Sel_shape_dir "Decreasing"/"Increasing" directional sign), Sel_curvature_sd, Sel_devmag_sd. penalty Gaussian SSQ, switch_check() converts weight = 1/(2*sd^2). Legacy Sel_curve_pen values never overwritten (existing models bit-identical); fleet supplying SD columns fits equivalently. Sel_shape_sd / Sel_devmag_sd apply NonParametric (2/9) LogisticPM (11); Sel_curvature_sd NonParametric-(LogisticPM use Sel_curve_pen2). Setting SD column form doesn’t use slot weight (e.g. 2D/3D-AR1, reuse Sel_curve_pen logit-scale correlations), non-positive SD, errors clearly. Readable string aliases integer-coded switches. Following CIE review’s “rename options improve interpretability” (e.g. constant → estimated), integer-switches now also accept self-explanatory strings, resolved switch_check() (build_srr()) integer codes (fits identical). New aliases follow consistent convention — -estimated value "Fixed", estimated "Estimated": estDynamics: "Estimated" (0) / "Fixed" (1) / "FixedScaled" (2) / "FixedScaledByAge" (3); Estimate_index_sd / Estimate_catch_sd: "Fixed" (0) / "Estimated" (1) / "Analytical" (2); srr_est_mode (via build_srr()): "Fixed" (0) / "Estimated" (1) / "LognormalPrior" (2) / "BetaPrior" (3); suitMode: documented string map ("Empirical", "GammaWeight", …) now actually applied (previously defined never wired).

what: Environmental linkages: a unified, formula-driven API
title: Rceattle 4.1.0
text: new long-format linkage table lets users express process parameters depend environmental covariates stratifying factors (species, sex, age) single formula-driven helper, linkage_spec(). row table corresponds exactly one estimated coefficient. fit_mod() pools every spec shared design matrix X per-row parameter vector beta_linkage; TMB template iterates table accumulates per-process offsets linear predictor underlying parameter. New constructor: linkage_spec(). Captures (formula, , species, link, init, bounds, priors, est_phase) one process parameter. Anything model.matrix() understands works: ~ 1, ~ temp + PDO, ~ poly(temp, 4), ~ (temp^2), ~ splines::ns(temp, df = 4), ~ temp * PDO, etc. Per-species formulas. Register multiple specs parameter via linkages = list(log_K = list(spec_a, spec_b)) spec’s optional species = ... argument scoping subset stocks. pooler unions design columns across specs ’s duplication species share covariates. Priors. First-class via prior_normal(), prior_lognormal(), prior_gamma(), prior_beta(). constructors available unprefixed (normal() / lognormal() / …) inside priors = ... argument via private NSE data mask, user code stays close mathematical notation without masking base::gamma() / base::beta() package level. Priors can single value applied every species, named list keyed species id (shortly, (species, sex)). Bounds. Per-row lower / upper flow build_bounds()$lower$beta_linkage / build_bounds()$upper$beta_linkage. Growth (von Bertalanffy / Richards) first process fully wired new pipeline. build_growth() gains linkages argument string-named fun ("empirical" / "vonBertalanffy" / "Richards"); integer codes still work (fun = 1 shorthand fun = "vonBertalanffy") existing scripts don’t need rewritten apart substituting fun = growth_model =. TMB plumbing. New src/TMB/linkage.hpp accumulator; ceattle_v01_11.cpp reads parallel DATA_IVECTOR(linkage_*) inputs plus DATA_MATRIX(linkage_X) writes growth_linkage_offset tensor added (additively, log scale) growth_parameters. Per-row prior densities contribute slot 19 joint NLL (“Linkage-table priors” fit$quantities$jnll_comp). Documentation. New vignette vignette("environmental-linkages", package = "Rceattle") walks API, prior families, species-keyed priors, per-species formulas, basis-expansion formulas, underlying pipeline. Natural mortality second process wired pipeline. build_M1() gains linkages argument keyed log_M1; offset added log scale log_M1 inside M1_at_age compute. row’s age_bin == NA broadcasts offset across ages; specific values pin age slice. build_M1() also gains string-form acceptance M1_model M1_re (parity build_growth(fun)): Growth M can linked fit; rows share global linkage table beta_linkage parameter vector. Per-(species, sex) priors. addition scalar species-keyed priors, priors[[col]] value may two-level nested list keyed first species id sex id: Missing keys either level resolve “prior” stratum. validator checks structure recursively emits actionable error messages keyed priors$<col>$<species>[$<sex>] paths. Default = ~ species. linkage_spec() now defaults argument ~ species, linkage produces one coefficient per species without user spell . Pass ~ species + sex per-(species, sex) coefficients, = NULL share single coefficient across every species/sex (prior default). matches typical multispecies assessment use case stock environmental sensitivity. Recruitment third process wired pipeline. build_srr() gains linkages argument keyed log_R0, log_alpha, log_beta; offset added log scale corresponding parameter every recruitment compute call site (hindcast, BRPs, projections, expected R). log_R0 meaningful srr_fun; log_alpha log_beta work SRRs consume (srr_fun c(2, 3, 4, 5) – Beverton-Holt Ricker). Growth, M, recruitment can linked fit; rows share global linkage table beta_linkage parameter vector. End--end tests tests/testthat/tests-Dynamics/test-linkage-auto-map.R verify base parameter (e.g., log_growth_pars, log_M1, rec_pars) automatically mapped (set NA) linkage active parameter, allowing linkage intercept define base value. tests/testthat/tests-Dynamics/test-recruitment-linkage.R cover analytical relations R = R0 * exp(beta * temp[yr]) (mean R) growth + M + recruitment composition. Soft deprecation build_M1(). legacy column-index argument M1_indices env-driven structural integer codes M1_model %% c(4, 5) subsumed new linkages = list(log_M1 = ...) argument. still work one release cycle, emit one-time warning points users equivalent linkage-table call. string aliases "env_sex_invariant" / "env_sex_specific" (added briefly dev branch) removed; never released. cpp’s M1_beta / M1_mult code path stays place now – paths add additively log_M1 log scale – use coefficient double-count. Roadmap. Recruitment next pipeline; random-effects pooling re_group hierarchical shrinkage. legacy M1_indices / M1_model = 4|5 paths retire recruitment migrates.
code: build_growth(   fun = "vonBertalanffy",   linkages = list(     log_K = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ temp,       by      = ~ species + sex,       priors  = list(temp = normal(0, 1))     )   ) ) build_M1(M1_model = "sex_age_invariant",   # or 1          M1_re    = "ar1_age",             # or 4          linkages = list(            log_M1 = linkage_spec(formula = ~ temp, by = ~ species)          )) priors = list(   temp = list(     `1` = list(`1` = normal(0, 0.1),                `2` = normal(0, 0.2)),    # sp 1 by sex     `2` = normal(0, 0.5)                  # sp 2, both sexes   ) ) build_srr(   srr_fun  = 2,   linkages = list(     log_alpha = linkage_spec(formula = ~ temp,                              priors  = list(temp = normal(0, 0.5)))   ) )
